title: The History and Future of Social Technologies

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The History and Future of Social Technologies shows what histories of tools often overlook.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Behind a ship's cargo stand contracts, credit, and rules for settling disputes.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: These arrangements shape what machines make possible, and who benefits.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book follows this relationship from early cooperation to artificial intelligence.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its central question is whether people can correct the institutions coordinating their lives.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Consider an illustrative payment: the coin is present, but the seller refuses it.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The obstacle is recognition, rather than the coin's ability to change hands.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Monetary systems depend on shared units, accepted claims, and ways to settle balances.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book uses money to explain how strangers cooperate without knowing one another.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: But the same portable signals can give their issuers power over everyone depending on them.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The chapters on administration follow this bargain into records, offices, and unequal authority.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A receipt and an official ledger can disagree about the same payment.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book asks whether the affected person can inspect and challenge the record.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Keeping a record and correcting its consequences are different institutional abilities.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: This turns an old administrative problem into a test for digital systems.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its future chapters apply that test to platforms, executable rules, and AI judgment.
